decisions.reason: The firm publicly presented the citrus harvesting crate as a flagship of its sustainability direction, so dropping it would write off a visible investment and expose that choice as a mistake, and seasonal agricultural demand gives room to attribute weak results to temporary causes.
A multi-model foldable large container line with its own web page in both years represents substantial tooling investment and visible commitment in a core returnable-packaging segment.
Stackable crates are a core category with several models and heavy mould investment, so management would persist with the line rather than write off those sunk costs.
The rackable pallet line involves significant tooling across several models and fits the firm's core pallet business, which favours keeping it.
Its website presence fell from an own page to a mere mention, which suggests waning emphasis, but the multi-model line and its tooling investment still argue for persistence.

This single niche product lost its own page and carries little public commitment, making it the most likely to be dropped, though mould costs already incurred still tilt the decision toward keeping it for now.
